question_stem: Why did the court reject Santos’s argument that Kimmel’s use could not be transformative because Kimmel had "instigated" and effectively designed the original Cameo videos?
How did the court use Santos’s own pleadings to undermine his contention that his original purpose in making the videos matched Kimmel’s later purpose in airing them?
Why did the court conclude that Kimmel’s alleged deception in ordering the Cameo videos did not defeat the fair-use defense?
Why did the court find Santos’s asserted market harm insufficient under the fourth fair-use factor?
How did the court justify resolving fair use at the pleading stage rather than waiting for factual development?
Why did the court decline to decide whether Santos’s contract claims were preempted by the Copyright Act?
How did the court justify relying on copyright registrations during review of the Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal, and what role did those registrations play in the fair-use analysis?
How did the structure of the Cameo Terms of Service itself reinforce the court’s conclusion that Santos was not an intended third-party beneficiary of the provisions he relied on?
Why was Santos unable to maintain a direct breach-of-contract claim based on the Cameo Terms of Service?
Compare why Santos’s written-contract and implied-contract theories failed. How did the court treat them as deficient in different ways?
Under the court’s analysis, what additional allegations would have been necessary to make an implied-in-fact contract claim plausible?
Why did Santos’s implied-contract theory fail under New York law?
Based on the court’s reasoning, what would Santos have needed to identify in the Terms of Service to make his direct contract claim more plausible?
Why did Santos’s fraudulent-inducement claim fail even if Kimmel’s false identities induced Santos to record the videos?
